rv.q: This is all very good, and everything tonight is good, even if only some of it really thrills – that’s the necessary risk of new work.
And what Rambert is now is loud, fast, brash and rather superficial, if this fleetingly enjoyable take-away meal of an evening is what we have to go on.
It’s a pulsating, heady concoction that celebrates the unity that great dance can inspire.
It’s a sad ending to an otherwise wonderful evening.
It was a thrilling, beautiful and moving evening which really allows this talented company to shine.
The raw energy of this piece, animated by Pierre Aviat's assertive, pounding musical score, is contagious, and the dancers' sheer joy and togetherness make for a thrilling half-hour.
The piece feels intimate, showcasing the dancers' exquisite fluidity and linework, while flashes of humour emerge through sharp, staccato gestures.

cn.t: Rambert's centenary celebration earns praise for its forward-looking vision and high-impact choreography, though critics are divided on execution. The triple bill showcases the company's contemporary ambition rather than nostalgia.
